name: Basilica of St. Mary Star of the Sea
history: Spanish Jesuits established a Catholic presence in the Keys on Upper Matecumbe Key in 1566. Key West's first permanent church was dedicated on 26 February 1852, the first parish in South Florida. It burned in 1901, and the present church was built in 1905. It is the oldest parish in the Archdiocese of Miami and became a basilica in 2012.
arch: Eclectic Victorian with early Renaissance Revival touches: rusticated walls, round arches, louvered shutters and coloured glass, under two front towers.
features: A stained glass window behind the altar shows Mary, Star of the Sea.
The parish ran the first Catholic school in Florida.

look.d: White spires above the palms of Truman Avenue.
Shutters and arches suit the island heat.

fun: Its patroness, Star of the Sea, is a traditional title of Mary for sailors.
journal: Southernmost basilica in the country. Shutters open to the sea breeze.

quiz.q: Which title of Mary is the patroness?
Who first brought Catholicism to the Keys in 1566?
